titulo: Anatomy of a video prompt: subject, action, camera, light and sound
lead: A video prompt is the shot-list line written for the machine. Who it is, what they do, where, how the camera sees it, what light, and what you hear. Now that sound comes out together with the image, it goes in the prompt too, in a separate sentence.
objetivo: write the prompt for a shot in seven parts, with the sound in a separate sentence and what to avoid described without "no".

aprende.t: The seven parts of a video prompt and their order
Swap a still verb for a living verb
Put sound and dialogue in the prompt the way the generator understands
Describe what to avoid without using "no"

hero_alt: A dark directing desk seen from above, with a closed notebook, studio headphones, a clapperboard and a stopwatch under a cool lamp.

secoes.titulo: The seven parts of the prompt
secoes.sub: Not every prompt uses all of them, but each one answers a question. Tap each part.

nos.detalhe: The focus of the shot, with concrete detail. "A 58-year-old baker, hair in a bun under a scarf, navy-blue apron" instead of "a woman". The character comes from the character sheet in course 0.
What happens right now, with a verb that tells a story: "kneads the dough", "opens the oven door". Still verbs ("standing", "posing", "looking at the camera") leave the generator to invent the rest.
Place and time with one or two details that only this place has: "neighborhood bakery at 4:50 a.m., white tiles, dark street outside".
Size, angle and one movement, in the terms of course 0. You don't invent anything here: you copy it from the shot list line.
The look card from course 0, the same in every prompt of the scene. It is what makes the shots look like they belong to the same film.
Ambience, effect and dialogue, in sentences separate from the image. Dialogue in the format "who says: text".
What you don't want to see, described as a thing: "on-screen text, watermark". Google's guide advises against writing "don't show".

secoes.legenda: Practical order: what you see first (subject, action, setting), then how you see it (camera, light), then what you hear.

secoes.sub: The example is shot 4 of "The first batch": the oven door opens and the steam rises.

texto: Start with what a viewer would understand in one second: who, doing what, where. Swap generic adjectives for detail that only exists in this scene.
A living verb carries the story: "the iron door opens slowly and the steam rises against the light" says more than "an oven in a bakery".

exemplo.texto: "bakery oven" → "the iron door of a deck oven opens slowly and the steam rises against the light"

passos.sub: from the shot list and the look
texto: Size, angle and movement are on the shot's line in your shot list. The light is on the look card. Copy, don't rewrite: that's what keeps the scene consistent.
If you don't have these files yet, do lessons 2 to 4 and 7 of course 0 first.

exemplo.texto: 4 | close-up | low angle | dolly in | 4 s → "Close-up, low angle, slow dolly in."

texto: Google's official video prompt guide (Veo and Gemini Omni Flash, updated on 10/15/2026) recommends saying clearly that you want audio and describing it in separate sentences: effects, ambient sound and dialogue.
The guide, in English, writes who speaks, "says:" and the text. In Portuguese, this course uses "who says: text". A short sentence fits in the shot; a paragraph doesn't.

exemplo.texto: Three knocks on the iron door. The baker says: Coming! In the background, the radio, low.

texto: In the negative prompt field, list what you don't want as things: "on-screen text, watermark, people in the background". The same guide advises against "no" instructions, like "don't show text".
There's no consensus on the ideal prompt length: sources range from 10 to 150 words. Start complete and cut what the generator ignores.

secoes.sub: The prompt sheet that the page checks, and the request for the AI assistant to put everything into one flowing text.

blocos.conteudo:
Subject: <who or what, with detail from the character sheet>
Action: <what happens, with a lively verb>
Setting: <where and when, with one detail unique to that place>
Camera: <size, angle and one movement, from the shot list>
Light: <your look card>
Sound: <ambient sound, effect and dialogue in the format "who says: text">
Avoid: <things you don't want to see, without "no">
Prompt: <the parts above in one flowing text, with the sound in a separate sentence>

blocos.rot: Request for the AI assistant (put the prompt together)

secoes.exemplo:
Subject: the iron door of a deck oven in a neighborhood bakery
Action: the door slowly opens and steam rises against the light
Setting: small bakery at 4:50 a.m., white tile, dark street outside
Camera: close-up, low camera, slow dolly in
Light: low-key, side light from the oven, steam in the beam; cold, dark street
Sound: creak of the oven door and hiss of steam; low radio in the background
Avoid: on-screen text, watermark, people in the background
Prompt: Close-up, low camera: in a neighborhood bakery at 4:50 a.m., the iron door of a deck oven slowly opens and steam rises against the oven's side light. Slow dolly in. Low-key, white tile, cold, dark street through the shop window. Sound: creak of the oven door and hiss of steam. In the background, a low radio.
secoes.exemplo_errado:
Subject: an oven
Action: opening
Setting: bakery
Camera: close-up, low camera
Light: beautiful
Prompt: bakery oven opening, cinematic, do not show text

secoes.sub: Only for people who already use a terminal. Download the course from GitHub and run it in its folder: the rules are the same as on the page. For your own file, replace --exemplo with its name (prompt.txt); it exits 0 when it passes.

python3 conferir.py prompt --exemplo; echo "saída: $?"

secoes.sub: A shot from your shot list, preferably one with a striking sound.

exercicios.titulo: Prompt · one shot in eight lines
exercicios.texto: Pick a shot from your shot list. Fill in the prompt.txt using the template: camera copied from the shot list, light copied from the look card, sound in a separate sentence. If you like, ask the AI assistant to put the flowing text together, and review it. Paste it into "Check your prompt" and download the file to the project folder.
exercicios.pronto: the page answers OK: prompt with 8 parts and the prompt.txt is in the project folder.

exercicios.texto: Read the Avoid line and the Prompt line. Replace every sentence with "no" or "don't" ("don't show text", "no people") with things listed out ("on-screen text, people in the background") and check again.
exercicios.pronto: the page keeps answering OK: prompt with 8 parts and the words "no" and "don't" do not appear in the Avoid line.

secoes.sub: Four questions. The explanation shows up after each answer.

perguntas.p: Which action leaves the least for the generator to invent?
opcoes: A baker standing in the bakery, looking at the camera.
A baker posing next to the bakery oven.
A good-looking baker in a cinematic bakery.
The baker takes out the first batch with the wooden peel.
perguntas.explica: Active verbs say what happens and narrow the generator's choices. "Standing," "posing," and adjectives like "beautiful" or "cinematic" say nothing the machine can act on.

perguntas.p: How does Google's official guide recommend putting sound in the prompt?
opcoes: Say you want audio and describe it in sentences separate from the image.
Write the sound in square brackets at the start of the prompt.
Leave sound out of the prompt completely and add everything later, in the edit.
Use only the words "cinematic sound" at the end of the prompt.
perguntas.explica: The guide says to make it clear you want audio and to describe effects, ambient sound, and dialogue in their own sentences. Keeping the sound separate also makes it easy to swap just that part on a new attempt.

perguntas.p: You don't want any text on screen. What do you write in the negative prompt field?
opcoes: "Don't show any text on screen, please."
"No text, no letters, and nothing written."
perguntas.explica: The guide recommends describing what you don't want as a thing, without "don't" or "no": the field itself already says it's for avoiding. Writing "don't show" is exactly what it advises against.

perguntas.p: Where do the camera and light in a shot's prompt come from?
opcoes: From the automatic suggestion the generator makes after the first attempt.
From a ready-made prompt copied from another creator who made something similar.
From the shot's line in the shot list and the scene's look card.
From the style of a famous director, named in the prompt.
perguntas.explica: Camera and light were decided in course 0, for the whole scene. Copying from the shot list and the look keeps the shots consistent. Naming a director imitates a real person's work; describe the ingredients of the look instead.

itens.texto: Subject, action, setting, camera, light, sound, and avoid. Then, the running text.
Ambient sound, effect, and dialogue in their own sentences; dialogue as "who says: text".
List things in the negative field, as Google's guide recommends.
